notes:
SCOPE: per the S.N.218 brief note, scoped strictly to Costco's Home/Decor-relevant category pages (Home Decor rollup + the decor-relevant part of the separate Lighting & Ceiling Light Fixtures line, which Costco's own site files under its Home Improvement department, not Home & Decor - included anyway per this project's universal Lighting-is-in-scope rule, same treatment Target US/S.N.22 and Bed Bath & Beyond/S.N.47 gave their own lighting trees) - did not enumerate Electronics, Grocery, Tires, Furniture, Appliances, Auto, etc.

ACCESS: robots.txt (https://www.costco.com/robots.txt) checked first - no Claude-specific disallow (ClaudeBot/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot/Claude-Web are not mentioned at all); only generic legacy-WCS view-pattern disallows (CategoryDisplay*, CatalogSearch*, ProductDisplay* etc.), which per Rule 3 are not a block signal. The homepage (https://www.costco.com/) fetches cleanly (HTTP 200, direct urllib, no special headers) every time, confirming the site is live and not retired. However EVERY other path tested this session - every department .html page (home-and-decor.html, furniture.html, appliances.html, electronics.html, patio-lawn-garden.html) and every decor leaf page (mirrors.html, wall-art.html, lighting.html, candles.html, etc.) - is hard-blocked, exhausting Rule 2: (1) direct fetch (urllib, requests, probe.py) -> HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai edge/WAF block, errors.edgesuite.net reference) on every profile/session, including a session that had just successfully fetched the homepage and carried its Akamai cookies (akavpau_zezxapz5yf, _abck, bm_s/bm_so/bm_sz); (2) curl_cffi impersonation sweep of 19 browser profiles (chrome99/100/110/116/119/120/123/124/131/133a, edge99/101, safari15_3/15_5/17_0/18_0, firefox133/135) - all either the same WAF 403, or (safari15_3/15_5/17_0 specifically) a 200-status Akamai Bot Manager behavioural-sensor interstitial ('sec-if-cpt-container' / 'Powered and protected by Akamai') that requires executing obfuscated JS to pass, which browser automation is off-limits for on this project; (3) r.jina.ai reader proxy -> itself hit a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' managed challenge before ever reaching costco.com; (4) translate.goog (www-costco-com.translate.goog) -> unlike on Bed Bath & Beyond (S.N.47) this side door did reach a genuine costco.com origin (real ServerName/build-number meta tags, Costco favicon) but that origin returned a plain 'Page Not Found!' 404 for every path tried (root, appliances.html, furniture.html, home-and-decor.html alike) - the translate.goog client apparently gets routed to a legacy WCS surface that doesn't recognise the modern Next.js pretty-URL routes, a dead end; (5) WebFetch -> timed out (60s) or ECONNRESET on every department/decor page AND on the homepage itself, so this tool could not reach costco.com at all this session; (6) side doors - sitemap_lw_index.xml/sitemap_lw_c_000.xml (top-level department sitemap) fetch cleanly as plain XML/static assets and were the source of the home-and-decor.html department URL and confirmed the department roster; static Next.js JS bundle chunks also fetch cleanly (200) but contain no client-exposed category/count API endpoint (SSR is server-side only). No Akamai sensor solver exists for this platform (the project's inditex_interstitial_solver.py targets a different, simpler exposed-math-puzzle challenge, not Akamai's obfuscated device-fingerprint sensor used here). Independent confirmation this is a systemic, well-known block: a live web search for scraping guidance on costco.com surfaced multiple 2025-era vendor writeups (ScrapingBee, Unwrangle, Apify) all independently stating Akamai blocks Scrapy/Playwright/Selenium/etc. on costco.com and that JS rendering plus residential proxies are required, matching what was found here - a genuine hard block, not a fixable configuration issue this session, same category of block as the S.N.75 Lowe's precedent (also Akamai) referenced in the brief.

STRUCTURE SOURCE (since live pages are unreachable): the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (structure only per Rule 2 - its counts are explicitly NOT used as qty anywhere in this file, consistent with the brief's warning that a warehouse-club's inventory-driven, rotating-SKU counts would likely be stale within months) has clean full-size captures of every decor leaf page from 2024-12-01/12-31 (close in time to each other, used for internal facet-count cross-checks only, never as live evidence). Each Costco category page is built on a WCS/LucidWorks-style storefront whose left-rail 'Category' facet panel lists the page's own child sub-categories (each an independent .html leaf with its own canonical URL) - this facet panel is what supplied every sub_category name and canonical link in this file. home-decor.html itself is a mixed ROLLUP, not a genuine leaf: its Dec-2024 Category facet broke down into exactly the set of children below (historical facet counts, NOT used as qty) - Artificial Plants/Flowers/Trees, Candles & Candle Holders, Clocks & Weather Stations, Curtains & Drapes, Digital Picture Frames, Home & Decorative Accents, Lamps, Mirrors, Slipcovers, Throw & Decorative Pillows, Wall Art, Wall Decor - and its own historical total (117) approximately equalled the sum of those children (118, small variance = normal inventory churn between snapshot crawls), confirming it is a pure union/rollup and should not itself be emitted as a leaf row. Likewise lighting.html is a rollup of Light Bulbs/Ceiling Fans/Chandeliers/Flush & Semi-Flush Mount Lighting/Landscape/Outdoor Lighting/Pendant Lighting/Vanity & Bathroom Lighting, and wall-art.html (itself just 3 Costco Next vendor-showcase tiles, a NEVER-EXTRACT 'Brands' page, not real product tiles) rolls up Art Prints and Canvas Art.

EXCLUDED FROM THE ROLLUPS PER STANDARD SCOPE RULES: Light Bulbs, Ceiling Fans (Lighting rollup - bulbs/fans excluded categories); Artificial Plants/Flowers/Trees (faux plants exclusion), Curtains & Drapes (textiles/window-treatment exclusion - distinct from curtain RODS which Costco does not appear to sell as a separate decor line), Digital Picture Frames (an electronics/smart-display gadget, not a decor picture frame), Slipcovers and Throw & Decorative Pillows (textiles/furniture-cover exclusions) - all from the Home Decor rollup. Also excluded as out-of-scope adjacent pages found in the sitewide link sweep but not pursued further: floral-centerpieces.html (silk/fresh floral arrangements, same family as the already-excluded artificial-plants line) and garden-center-ponds-fountains.html (filed under Patio/Garden Center, product-title spot-checks of similar Costco garden pages suggest this is pond-equipment/liners/pumps rather than purely decorative fountains) and nursery-furniture-decor.html (baby-nursery furniture-dominated, not general home decor).

DROPPED AS AN UNSPLITTABLE MIXED ROLLUP (Rule: 'mixed roll-ups: drop, don't pad'): Candles & Candle Holders (candles.html). Its Dec-2024 snapshot showed 'Showing 1-13 of 13' - i.e. the sampled product-title list IS the complete historical inventory, not a partial sample - and of those 13, 11 are Home-Fragrance-exclusion items (Sand+Fog/Antiga 1860/Apotheke-brand wax candles - luxury fragrance-house brands whose Costco listings are explicitly scented per their own product lines -, 2 reed/oil diffusers, 1 wax warmer, 1 holiday gift set) and only 2 (LumiPur 25-piece and 15-piece Flameless LED Candle sets) plus arguably 1 borderline item (Mikasa Electric Candle Warmer Lamp) are genuinely in-scope unscented/flameless decor. Unlike Target or BBB, Costco has no separate 'Candle Holders' or 'Flameless Candles' leaf URL to isolate the in-scope minority - candles.html is the only candle-bearing page site-wide - so including it wholesale would misrepresent an 85%-Home-Fragrance bucket as a decor category; it was dropped rather than padded.

KEPT BUT FLAGGED AS MIXED (genuine in-scope product type exists, but the single Costco page mixes in excluded types with no way to isolate a clean sub-count without live access): Clocks (weather-stations-clocks.html) - its complete Dec-2024 3-item inventory was 1 genuine alarm clock plus a Bluetooth sound machine and a wireless weather station (both excluded, non-decor electronics) - Clocks stays in scope per the brief's explicit 'Clocks (all types)' inclusion, since a real clock product type does exist there, but the page itself is not clock-exclusive. Decorative Accents (decorative-accents.html) - complete Dec-2024 14-item inventory was dominated by 6 poufs (furniture/textile, excluded) and 2 smart-electronics items (digital picture frame, smart calendar), with only 2 jewelry boxes and 1 figurine (Fitz & Floyd Nutcracker) clearly in-scope decorative accessories, plus one borderline seasonal item (Glass Pumpkin LED candles, leaning Holiday-exclusion) - kept because 'decorative accessories/figurines' is a core project include-category and genuine qualifying items were found, but flagged given the low in-scope fraction. Outdoor Decor (outdoor-decor.html) - complete Dec-2024 23-item inventory was majority (about 19 of 23) genuine Desert Steel-brand metal garden sculptures/statues plus a copper bird bath and patio torches (all in scope per the brief's decorative-metal/sculpture inclusion and the Target-precedent Outdoor Torches/Garden Sculptures treatment), with a minority excluded as functional (stone stepping stones, a privacy screen panel, a Solo Stove fire-bowl cooking appliance) - kept, majority in-scope.

Every qty below is null because no live count could be obtained this session despite exhausting Rule 2 (see ACCESS above); every row instead carries a MANUAL REVIEW flag. Wayback-derived historical facet counts are cited in evidence purely as structural corroboration of each sub-category's existence and are explicitly NOT used as the qty value, per Rule 2 and the brief's specific warning that Costco's rotating warehouse-club SKUs make any non-live count unreliable.
